setup: Squaring the equation [[fn]] x = c, with a positive c below 1, produces extra solutions on an interval of [[N]] turns.

steps.say: Squaring turns the right side into c squared, and both [[fn]] x = c and [[fn]] x = -c satisfy the squared equation.
The negative branch mirrors the positive one, so each genuine solution gains a partner in the same turn.
The pattern repeats in each of the [[N]] turns, so the extraneous count equals the count of genuine solutions.
